chunks: O the negligent, who are not forgiven, and the abandoners, from whom [their deeds] will be taken,
What is it that I see you departing from Allah and desiring others?
You are like camels upon which a herdsman has driven [them] to a pasture that is diseased, and a watering place that is disastrous,
And indeed they are like beasts that are fed in order to be slaughtered, but they do not know what is intended for them!
When treated well, they consider their day to be their whole life, and their fullness to be their aim.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of the camel used to describe human negligence in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs the vivid metaphor of livestock fattened for slaughter to critique the spiritual complacency of the neglectful, a theme central to Shia eschatological thought regarding the deception of dunya. This passage underscores the scholarly distinction between mere physical sustenance and true divine purpose, warning that temporary worldly comfort often masks the inevitability of the Hereafter.
